relationships.external_proposition: Enforce approved logical-access authorisations for information and system resources under the applicable access-control policies.
relationships.invariant: Protected information must remain within the independently established authorisation boundary for access, acquisition, disclosure and modification. Technical reachability, absent authentication or ineffective access restrictions must not permit an unauthorised information operation.
relationships.supported_component: Direct support for enforcing approved logical-access boundaries. The VIGIL property also covers observed disclosure and modification; the source does not define VIGIL occurrence recognition.

actors: Organisation implementing selected security and privacy controls
objects: Information and system resources subject to logical access
conditions: Approved authorisations and applicable access-control policies govern the access.
qualifications: Catalogue controls are selected and tailored for the organisation and system. Presence in the catalogue does not make every control universally applicable.
Nongovernmental use is voluntary. Independent legal, policy or contractual obligations require separate applicability analysis.
The imperative is a control expectation if selected; it is not a VIGIL classification condition.

relationships.limitation: Source controls support stated components, not the entire VIGIL recognition contract. Candidate identity and canonical admission remain pending.

actors: Identity provider or authorisation server in the report’s federal environment and signed-token scope
conditions: Federally scoped identity/access systems using asymmetric signed tokens or assertions; see §1.1.

Section 1.2 makes MUST a conformance condition, while conformance remains voluntary absent applicable policy or binding agreement.
Ordinary API keys, symmetric schemes and stateful management are outside the controls’ scope; no direct mapping from these provisions to Moltbook API tokens or DeepSeek API secrets is asserted.
